    Breads

    Shokupan

    There's nothing quite like tearing into a loaf of shokupan still warm from the oven: soft, pillowy, faintly sweet and impossibly light. Baked in a lidded 1.5 kin shokupan loaf pan (20 × 12 × 12.5 cm) for a flat top, or without the lid for a rounded one. It's the bread for the Egg Sando.

    Serves 1 loaf (about 10 slices)Prep 1 hr + 2 hr 30 min risingCook 30 min
    Vegetarian

    Chicken

    Chicken Nanban

    Crisp, tangy and creamy all in one bite. Egg-coated fried chicken is soaked in a sweet and sour nanban sauce, then topped with a generous spoonful of rich tartar sauce.

    Serves 3Prep 20 minCook 15 min

    Karaage

    Golden, crackling pieces of chicken that rarely make it from the rack to the plate. Marinated in ginger, garlic and soy, then fried twice for a light, crisp crust and a juicy middle.

    Serves 4Prep 15 min + 30 min marinatingCook 15 min
    Party food

    Katsu Curry

    A big, warming plate of comfort for a rainy night. Crisp crumbed chicken on rice, smothered in a rich, glossy Japanese curry sauce made from Golden Curry blocks. The cutlets are made exactly as for Tonkatsu.

    Serves 4Prep 20 minCook 30 min

    Tebasaki Wings

    Sticky, sweet and peppery, these are the wings you'll lick your fingers clean of. Double-fried and glazed in a soy, mirin and ginger sauce, then finished with a shower of sesame seeds. The sauce keeps in the fridge for a month.

    Serves 4Prep 20 minCook 30 min
    Party food

    Eggs

    Egg Sando

    The humble Japanese convenience-store sandwich that's somehow better than it has any right to be. Creamy Kewpie egg salad is mounded into soft, crustless Shokupan and cut on the diagonal.

    Serves 3Prep 5 minCook 10 min
    VegetarianUnder 30 min

    Ramen Eggs

    The little luxury that makes a bowl of ramen feel special. Soft-boiled eggs with jammy, golden yolks are marinated overnight in a sweet soy sauce. Add them to ramen or rice bowls, or eat them on their own.

    Serves 4 eggsPrep 5 minCook 7 min + 8–10 hr marinating
    Make ahead

    Pork

    Tonkatsu

    The crunch as the knife goes through is half the pleasure. Crumbed and fried pork (or chicken) cutlets, crisp outside and juicy inside, served with rice, a dab of mustard, pickled ginger and tonkatsu sauce.

    Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 15 min
    Under 30 min
